The friendly story lives in docs/project-journey-report.md (final-vs-now, mind-map, brackets, decision graph); the build order lives in docs/roadmap.md. Terms in (brackets) match the journey doc's glossary.

1. Project identity

Plain words: a classroom of laptops becomes a robot school with no cloud. Strong laptops (Hosts) share power and run sealed robot boxes; weak laptops (Guests) just use a browser; one laptop (Master) organizes.

LDNDRC (Local Dynamic Node Discovery ROS Cluster) is a local-first, browser-accessible robotics simulation platform: consumer laptops form a K3s cluster (K3s: lightweight organizer deciding what runs where), strong laptops ("Hosts") run isolated per-user ROS 2 workspaces (ROS 2: robot brain; workspace: sealed box with editor + sim + desktop), weak laptops ("Guests") use a browser. No cloud, no dedicated servers.

2. Architecture as built

Plain words: your laptop talks to the front door, the desk checks your wristband and serves the website, the organizer starts your sealed box, and you can peek through the glass wall.

text
Guest browser / joining laptop (same Wi-Fi, nicknames in hosts file)
  │  editor|desktop|gazebo|control .ros-platform.local → Traefik :80/:443 (front door)
  ▼
Control panel / desk (Go program, runs on the organizer's own network, modest container)
  ├─ /api/auth/*          login: JWT pass (signed proof) + wristband cookie + click stamp (R3)
  ├─ /api/sessions/*      boxes: create/list/stop, yours only, written in the notebook (R2)
  ├─ /api/nodes/*         welcoming: ask/wait/approve/deny/list/health-report
  ├─ /                   website inside the desk file (R4: Login/Launch/Workspace/Desktop/Admin)
  └─ gateway (guard)      checks wristband, forwards to your box's doors (FQDN dot: full address with trailing dot)
K3s API (organizer's controls, driven with client-go: the Go remote): per-box
  Deployment (recipe) + Service (address, doors 7682/8080/9002) + home PVC (5GB private disk);
  join tickets as Secrets (15-min passwords); laptop labels; health checks; restart re-read
Headlamp (glass wall, token key): operator sees everything
mDNS (Wi-Fi shout "_ldndrc-master._tcp"): organizer announces itself on hari:8082

Key facts, precisely: one Deployment + Service + PVC per box with a unique ROS_DOMAIN_ID (channel number so boxes can't hear each other) and ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST (robots talk inside their own box only); Host-only placing via node-role.kubernetes.io/role (label: this laptop shares power); graphics optional (SESSION_GPU_LIMIT=0 on plain-CPU today, "1" on NVIDIA hosts); browsers use wristband cookie + X-CSRF-Token stamp on changes, scripts use Bearer pass; box addresses dialed as FQDN (trailing dot — skips the Wi-Fi's wildcard-DNS trap found in CP20); organizer updates use delete-old-first (door :8082 fits one copy); picture tarballs imported from $HOME (2.4GB packed; /tmp too small/wiped).

3.3 Robot-world picture (images/)

Plain words: the frozen 10.8GB hard drive every sealed box boots from — robot brain, 3D physics, editor, screen sharing, practice models included.

Layer Contents State
images/base Ubuntu + Jazzy brain (desktop, navigation, robot↔3D bridge, TurtleBot3 drivers), chatter locked to localhost, student user 1000 Built 8.25GB, done
images/workspace Browser editor + 3D data pipe + screen manager + home starter (+ Fuel seed 64K: Ground Plane + Sun practice models) + Selkies 2.0.0 (WITH_SELKIES=1 switch) Built 10.8GB, live (:jazzy-harmonic-10f1f10c)
Tags Frozen :jazzy-harmonic-<code> (eaaf8088 → 4aa29d15 → 10f1f10c), never moving :latest Done; 2.4GB pack in $HOME

History kept: Selkies 1.6.2 files vanished upstream (404) → shipped without desktop, then moved to pure-Python 2.0.0 (no video-toolkit, sound-off is a native switch). Packing math (CP38): ~4.5x squeeze, import 164s cold → 28s warm (shared layers), Wi-Fi 1–4 min + unpack 1–3 min ≈ 5–10 min per new laptop once, then kept; shelf-mirror worth it at ~5 laptops.

Live on the real organizer (seen, not faked)

Plain words: a human watched it happen on the real laptop hari.

  • Move-in (CP20): permissions + recovered login secret + organizer-network + Wi-Fi shout + front door on 4 names (192.168.1.37); box starting→ready; editor OK first time here; first shout heard. Two bugs found only here: full-address dot (wildcard-DNS trap), delete-old-first (update deadlock).
  • Safety+memory (CP21): stamp matrix (no stamp → blocked, wrong → blocked, script pass → through) + editor still OK; killed container kept the same box ID, starting→ready on first visit, zero lost.
  • Website (CP24/26): pages 200 with the real bundle; login gives pass+stamp+wristband; Launch waiting → ready (3rd check); editor-OK / desktop-then-200 / 401 / 403 all hold; /admin 200 with cards; approve/deny round-trip on live rows (verify-laptop-a/b); delete → stopped feeds the filter chips.
  • Real world (CP33/35/37): ready ~20s (no download); editor redirect→IDE; desktop 200 screen page (502 era over); sim-data door answers with data; turtlebot3-sim empty in-box with zero download errors, full message bus, clock at full speed on plain CPU; seed present in home.
  • Merge (CP39): format/vet clean, 7 packs ok, 47-part bundle identical, recipe carries new picture + notebook setting.
  • Carried over: two-student walls + 403s, scheduler muscle/GPU refusals, full cleanup on delete, ticket-once over Wi-Fi, --plain 4/4, screen q→clean exit, permission probes, release checksum installs, test-join.sh 4/4, secret scans clean (fakes only).

7. Known limits (nothing hidden)

  • Login small bug (arrived CP39): old-wristband login attempt → 403. Next: skip stamp check on login.
  • Small restarts safe; whole-copy redeploys still lose track (notebooks on temporary shelf — full-memory step moves them to disk; graceful-update flag still default).
  • Recipe comment stale ("Selkies waiting/502", really 200-live).
  • No pretty sim viewer yet (data frame today).
  • No guest full-join yet (practice cluster couldn't take real agents; real organizer waits for the paired run). Guest hearing the shout pending.
  • No encryption yet (trusted Wi-Fi assumed); click-stamps are the only browser armor so far (R7: encryption, walls, limits, graphs).
  • Windows/WSL2 unproven on hardware; shelf-mirror/pre-load measured (CP38) not built; slimming/speed-packing parked; light picture parked.
  • Old bash join path still the only complete end-to-end road.

8. Remaining work (ordered — same as roadmap §2/§3)

  1. Login fix (< 0.5 day): skip login in stamp guard + test + rebuild + delete-old-first rollout + live proof; tidy stale Selkies line.
  2. Full memory (0.5–2 days): notebooks → disk/DB; graceful desk updates; prove redeploy loses nothing.
  3. Pretty viewer (0.5 day): gzweb piece into the site; world/house smoke. Optional: see-everyone Admin feed; glass-wall teacher lock.
  4. Two-laptop join (days, second laptop): full acceptance run — ask → approve → ticket → real install → marked-joined → box runs there; no-path; shout hearing.
  5. Windows proof + docs sunset (days).
  6. Sturdy (ongoing): encryption, limits, walls, graphs, logs.
  7. Picture parallel: shelf-mirror/pre-load at ~5 laptops; graphics follow-up (SESSION_GPU_LIMIT=1 + device plugin).
